clue.text: A cracking place for meal, perhaps for rocket starter?

indicators.note: A is cracking the phrase, breaking into it and sitting inside

parts.note: lunch is one example of a meal
pad is slang for one's place or home

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a splendid spot to eat, perhaps as a starter before the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place for meal' is read as a pad for lunch, so the meal word comes first. 'starter' looks like a first course but means where a rocket starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket begins its flight from a launch platform, so it is the starting point of a rocket.

clue.text: Priest suppressing wicked dance

indicators.note: the priest's word holds down and contains the other piece, keeping it inside

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
wicked means bad

explanation.surface: A clergyman frowns on a sinful dance and tries to stamp it out.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Cinema staff shifting heroin for people involved in drugs

indicators.note: shifting here means getting rid of, so the letter is moved out of the word

parts.note: ushers show people to their seats in a cinema
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Cinema workers dealing heroin to drug-takers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting heroin' reads as selling drugs, but it means removing H from USHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug users are people who take drugs, so they are involved in drugs.

clue.text: Tanks and fliers coming under ex-Soviet grouping

indicators.note: in a down entry the birds are placed below the grouping, so they come after it

parts.note: the CIS, Commonwealth of Independent States, grouped former Soviet republics
terns are seabirds, so fliers

explanation.surface: Military tanks and aircraft come under the control of a post-Soviet alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks and fliers' paints armour and pilots; the tanks are water tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, as in a loft or above a toilet.

clue.text: Painting depicting heartless soldiers turned up in collection

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
of, as in a painting of something, means depicting it

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for soldiers is taken out

parts.note: a troop is a unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: A painting of soldiers lacking spirit turns up among an art collection.
explanation.walkthrough: OIL + OF + TROP (TROOP without its central O) gives OILOFTROP, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a collection, of drawings, documents or investments held together.

clue.text: Protest over nationalist bogeyman

indicators.note: in a down entry the protest sits over the next letter, so it comes first

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A protest about a nationalist figure who is cast as the villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogeyman is an evil spirit used to frighten people, which is what a demon is.

clue.text: Fruits that one takes out?

definitions.meaning: sweet brown fruits of a palm tree
people one escorts on romantic outings

explanation.surface: Which fruit does one take out for a picnic?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a palm's fruit and a romantic partner for an evening out.

clue.text: Finds fault with opening performances, but tenor must be good

indicators.note: the tenor letter must become the good letter, so one replaces the other

parts.note: debuts are first performances

explanation.surface: A critic picks holes in first nights, but grants the tenor must be good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finds fault with' reads as criticising; here it means locating faults in software and removing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Debugging is locating and removing errors from program code, so it finds the faults in it.

clue.text: Figure outrageously paid zero tax initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word tax
outrageously, wildly, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tax figure in which someone outrageously paid nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a sum of money in a tax return, but it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapezoid is a geometric shape, a four-sided figure with one or no parallel sides.

clue.text: To inhale endless seaweed mostly provides source of inspiration at sea

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to snort is to inhale sharply through the nose

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed

explanation.surface: A swimmer breathing in seaweed finds it is the source of their troubles at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOR (SNORT without its end) plus KEL (most of KELP). 'inspiration' is literally breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a tube letting a swimmer breathe in, so a source of inhaled air underwater.

clue.text: Malts mixed with more water being circulated

indicators.note: mixed signals the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Malt whiskies mixed with extra water and swirled round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges MALTSMORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, so water whirling round and round.

clue.text: Applause in anticipation of Charlie?

definitions.meaning: a shout of approval or cheering
the NATO alphabet's B-word, which comes just before Charlie

explanation.surface: Clapping in expectation of Charlie's arrival on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for B immediately precedes Charlie for C.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouted at a performance, the Italian cry is a call of acclaim; in radio code it stands just ahead of Charlie.

clue.text: I'll read out a key passage

indicators.note: read out means the word is spoken, so it is judged by its sound

parts.note: the contraction of I will, pronounced like eye-ll

explanation.surface: Someone promises to read aloud an important passage of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a key' also gives A + ISLE, since a key is a low island, backing up the sound. 'passage' looks like a piece of text but is a walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a main route through a church or plane.

clue.text: Chinese change united European culinary product

parts.note: the fen is a small coin of China, a hundredth of a yuan
a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: A Chinese reform turns a united European dish into a product.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenugreek is an aromatic herb whose seeds and leaves are used in cooking, especially curries.

clue.text: Where size 12s are made, eventually?

definitions.meaning: on a long cobbler's foot-shaped mould, used for big shoes

explanation.surface: Wondering where huge shoes are made, when they finally are.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker builds a shoe round, so big shoes are made on a long one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means finally, after a long delay, which is what eventually means.

clue.text: Badly built car needs a drop of engine oil

indicators.note: badly built means the letters are put together wrongly, so rearranged
a drop of takes just a little, the first letter of engine

explanation.surface: A shoddily made car needs a drop of engine oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges BUILTCAR into LUBRICAT, then E from 'a drop of engine'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil a machine is to apply grease or oil so parts move freely.

clue.text: Psycho crushed insect, one crawling

indicators.note: crushed means the word's letters are squashed into a new order

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A madman squashed a creeping bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges PSYCHO into SYCOPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady who flatters to win favour is said to crawl, so a crawler or bootlicker.

clue.text: Prince perhaps said to get turbulent

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so it is judged by its sound

parts.note: a prince is an example of a royal

explanation.surface: A prince is reported to become unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: To roil is to become agitated or churned up, as muddy water does.

clue.text: Bird ready for fluent repetition after drinking firewater

indicators.note: drinking means the word takes the spirit inside it

parts.note: off pat means learnt and ready to be repeated fluently
rakee, a variant spelling of raki, is a strong anise spirit

explanation.surface: A talking bird is ready to chatter fluently once it has had a drink of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Firewater is slang for strong liquor; off pat means memorised, ready to be repeated fluently.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Brexiteer at heart, caught in very Remain atmosphere

indicators.note: the middle letter is caught inside the other letters

parts.note: to be is to remain or exist

indicators.note: at heart picks the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Leave voter, deep down, is caught up in a pro-Remain mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remain' suggests the Brexit vote but simply means BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibe is the feeling or mood a place gives off, its atmosphere.

clue.text: Grasping relative's loathsome to be seen

indicators.note: grasping means the loathsome word holds the relative inside it

parts.note: vile means loathsome
a sib is a sibling, a relative; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A greedy relative is detestable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something visible can be seen, which is the sense of the phrase.

clue.text: To demand money before leaving is iffy

parts.note: to touch someone is to ask them for money
and, as in this and then that, means before
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Asking for cash before departing is a dubious move.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky and uncertain, whose outcome could go either way, is precarious.

clue.text: A blonde's ghastly, chummy address

indicators.note: ghastly, dreadful, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word blonde; the 's is is, a link

explanation.surface: A fair-haired person looks awful, says someone in a friendly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ghastly' rearranges ABLONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated, matey British form of address to a friend, like 'old chap'.

clue.text: Behind with payment as rise in base interest comes around

indicators.note: the abbreviation for interest comes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: int. is the abbreviation for interest

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a flower bed or seabed

explanation.surface: Someone falls behind on payments as a rise in the base interest rate comes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base interest' suggests the bank base rate, but base is a bed, and int. is a standard abbreviation for interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone owing money who has not yet paid is behind with payment.

clue.text: No dressing needed for this low fat hummus?

parts.note: skinny describes food that is low in fat, as in a skinny latte
hummus is an example of a dip, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A low-fat hummus that needs no dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like salad dressing beside the hummus, but it means clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A swim in the nude is one taken without any clothes on, so no getting dressed is needed.

clue.text: Democratic to lift less well-off in downturn

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting means the letters are read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: poor means less well-off, lacking money

explanation.surface: Democrats pledge to lift the poorer in an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: A droop is a sagging or decline, a turn downwards.

clue.text: Extra confused when left out

indicators.note: out means the letter for left is removed from the word

parts.note: addled means confused

explanation.surface: Something additional baffles someone when it is omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Added material is supplementary, laid on in addition.

clue.text: Short afternoon play

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram
A is short for afternoon, as in p.m. readings

explanation.surface: A brief play put on in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective but is a short, a measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, screen or radio.

clue.text: Steady couple

definitions.meaning: to steady oneself, to prepare for an impact
a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: A dependable pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace is to steady or support; a brace is also a pair, as of pheasants.

clue.text: Typically ordinary part of church to get cross

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in the old O level
the nave is the main body of a church
to rage is to get angry

explanation.surface: Members of an ordinary congregation usually get angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a norm, the phrase means usually or as a rule.

clue.text: Occurrence of character in Genesis and later books

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Book of Genesis
NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A figure appears in Genesis and again in later books.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening or incident, something that occurs.

clue.text: Jogger's nipple perhaps after exercise for one of Nancy's baps?

indicators.note: the nipple complaint comes after the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
jogger's nipple is a sore chafed nipple, a tit pain

explanation.surface: A runner's chafed nipple after a workout, likened to a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is a French city, so its bread roll is French; a bap is a British soft roll. 'baps' is also slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit pain is a French bread roll, so a French version of a bap.
